findings.name: musculoskeletal examination
findings.result: Inspection: several non-tender nodules on the left 1st, 3rd and 4th distal interphalangeal joints. Palpation: tenderness at the base of both thumbs; enlarged knees with pain on passive range of motion. Range of motion: crepitus in the knees during passive movement; no significant limitation of movement due to pain.

source_issues: Nodules are placed on the left '1st' distal interphalangeal joint, which does not exist (the thumb has a single interphalangeal joint).
'Does not smoke or drink alcohol excessively' is ambiguous in scope.
notes: The chief complaint names two complaints (wrist pain, knee pain), so both are opening facts; the 10-year duration applies to both and is a standalone fact (f003).
Each Secondary_Symptoms denial (swelling, digit colour change, mucous-membrane dryness, fever/chills) repeats the history; one fact each citing both. Fever and chills are split.
'Denies any constitutional symptoms such as fever or chills' and 'Systemic review is otherwise unremarkable' form one 'other symptoms' denial (f011) besides the explicit fever and chills facts.
The professional-athlete history (History, Past_Medical_History) and 'Retired' (Social_History) are one occupation fact.

The musculoskeletal examination is one record because the source organises it by technique (inspection, palpation, range of motion) across hands, wrists and knees; splitting by joint would need guessing which leaf sentence belongs to which joint.
